body:
MEASURED against the live store on 2026-08-17, from a request trace of Claude's own connector.

WHAT HAPPENS. The client reads the protected-resource document and then POSTs its dynamic
registration to `{authorization_server}/register`. Loam serves that door at `/oauth/register`. The
guessed path is unrouted, so it falls through to the mount router, where `register` reads as a MOUNT
NAME and every unauthenticated mount path answers the uniform 401 that hides which mounts exist. So a
client trying to introduce itself is told to authenticate first — on the one door whose entire job is
admitting a client that has no credentials yet. Registration fails and the connector dies with
`Couldn't register with <store>'s sign-in service`.

Observed twice in one session, and the client is inconsistent about it: at 15:11 it went straight to
the guessed `/register`; at 15:18 it read `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` first and used the
real path. Both shapes are real, so serving only the documented path serves fewer clients than it
could.

THE FIX: route `/register`, `/authorize` and `/token` to the doors already at `/oauth/*`. Purely
additive — three more spellings of three existing doors, no new authority, no new capability. A client
that reads the metadata is unaffected.

THE ONE THING NOT TO DO, and it is the whole reason this is subtle: DO NOT fix this by making
unrouted paths answer 404 instead of 401. That fallthrough is what closes the mount-existence oracle
§12/T78 shut on purpose — a prober who can tell `unrouted path` from `mount exists` reads the mount
table off the difference. The refusal stays uniform; these three paths simply stop being unrouted.

RAILS (new file, nothing frozen is touched):
1. `POST /register` with a valid body answers 201 and mints the same client the documented path does
   — assert the client_id resolves in `oauth.json` afterwards, not just the status.
2. `GET /authorize` with a registered client and a live PKCE challenge renders the login form, the
   same page the documented path renders.
3. `POST /token` reaches the token door — an invalid code answers the token door's own 400, never a
   mount refusal.
4. THE ORACLE HOLDS: an unrouted path that is NOT one of the three (`/nonsense`, `/registerx`) still
   answers the uniform 401 byte-for-byte, indistinguishable from a real mount's refusal. This is the
   rail that keeps the fix from becoming a leak.
5. The documented `/oauth/*` paths are unchanged, asserted at the same call.

TIER: repair. It adds spellings, not authority, and it restores a promise §37 already makes — that a
connector can register itself. Self-merges on green plus P5.

PART OF THE CONNECTOR ARC: this is one of four tickets that must land before the temporary debugging
proxy in front of Myk's store can be removed. The others are T177, T178 and T148's open half.

OVERTAKEN (stale sweep, 2026-08-25): PR #423 (commit 0d93510) landed the fix: src/server/oauth.ts on main derives bare /register, /authorize, /token aliases from the documented /oauth/* paths (oauth.ts:333-353), with the ticket's rail file test/server/oauth-bare-paths.test.ts (394 lines) including the oracle-holds comparison. Shard is still in .adlc/tickets/ and should be archived.
title: The OAuth doors are unreachable at the paths a real client guesses, and the guess meets a 401
